messages.subject: Re: Using RHIPE in production
parts:
Hi Gourav

I'll attempt to answer some of these questions.

First, about R in general:

R seems to be becoming more accepted in industry.  Several companies use R, and you can find some good discussion threads on this topic.  I guess the thing that makes people nervous is not having support if there are problems.  Companies like Revolution Analytics provide the "open-source support" model like Cloudera for Hadoop.  But for add-on packages and such, if there are problems and the developer doesn't address them, you might be stuck.

Which brings me to RHIPE.  RHIPE is a mature package but still going through change.  There is a lot of research going on around RHIPE (such as D&R as you mentioned), so things are evolving.  An increasing number of people are getting involved with development - I don't want to speak for Saptarshi but I would guess that he will always be the maintainer - it is his creation.  RHIPE is getting substantial use in the government and at research institutions - there are plenty of people depending on it such that if there are bugs, they will be fixed.  But "technical support" for your specific problems is pretty much limited to getting help on this forum.

What type of case study are you looking for?  We will have a book chapter published soon describing how RHIPE was used to do some analysis at our lab that I can point you to if you are interested.

Finally - yes, D&R algorithms and methods for both numerical and visual routines will be distributed in the open source.  We will post about them as they become available and ready for the general public.


On Wednesday, March 20, 2013 11:09:50 AM UTC-7, Gourav Sengupta wrote:
Hi,

I came across a lot of industry consultants and best practitioners of R.

What most of them suggested is that since R is not a solution to be used at Enterprise scale therefore they switch over to Mahout, vanilla MR or Scala while deploying their models developed in R into production environments.

So I had a few questions:
1. Are there any case studies available on use of R in Hadoop using RHIPE or is it just few of the solutions which only a few can use and maintain?
2. In future who is going to maintain and upgrade RHIPE (currently I think it is only Mr. Guha)?
3. Are the D & R algorithms for common data mining problems going to made available online?
4. How realistic are the above statements?


Regards,
Gourav

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Using RHIPE in production
parts:
On Tue, Apr 16, 2013 at 8:08 AM, Zubin Dowlaty <nat...@gmail.com> wrote:
We have been testing RMR in production, couple of Fortune 500 companies, using the RHADOOP package, it does okay, developers like the API and syntax, but hard to manage memory, as its a child to the JVM.  JVM needs to manage the memory.


I dont think this is the case. In both rhmr and rhipe, the JVM launches R as a subprocess. And the memory consumed by the suprocess can be
controlled by unix resource controllers.

at least in RHIPE, the Java side does not buffer key values before sending them, instead writing directly to the child process. Hence there should be little interference
from the JVM. Our child JVMs run with -Xmx768m.
 And the reduce nodes run with 1.5Gb

hth

Hi,

I do not think that my question was relating to the technical abilities of RHIPE, the technical proposition is proven and visible. What I was asking is that any company would want to invest its time and infrastructure and resources in products which is supported by a thriving community beyond the core team that created it, monitors and drives it. Example: HADOOP, R, LINUX, TALEND, Mobile Phone Apps, etc.

RHIPE is definitely serving a niche market but what is the community support that it is encouraging or developing?


Regards,
Gourav
